all	core: list	port: BLKLSTOP	# BLKLOP (toke.c:2160, :8342, :8351) returns BLKLSTOP: a list operator whose first argument is a block, which a list shape does not say; CORE.tpm's prototype \&@ reads as a list, and perl accepts `any { $_ } @l`. Deliberately not folded into LSTOP.
any	core: list	port: BLKLSTOP	# BLKLOP (toke.c:2160, :8342, :8351) returns BLKLSTOP: a list operator whose first argument is a block, which a list shape does not say; CORE.tpm's prototype \&@ reads as a list, and perl accepts `any { $_ } @l`. Deliberately not folded into LSTOP.
catch	core: niladic	port: none	# a keyword, PREBLOCK(KW_CATCH) (toke.c:8370); not a function, so CORE.tpm's niladic shape is the parser's own and the port has no builtin class for it.
do	core: unary	port: none	# KW_DO (yyl_do, toke.c:8445), a block or a file expression with its own rules in perly.y; the port classes it as a keyword, not UNIOP.
dump	core: niladic	port: none	# LOOPEX (LOOPX, toke.c:257, :8471), a loop-exit word that forces its label; perl -c refuses the bare form (`dump() must be written as CORE::dump()`).
goto	core: unary	port: none	# LOOPEX (LOOPX, toke.c:257, :8587), a loop-exit word that forces its label or takes a term; the port classes it as the loop exit, not UNIOP.
isa	core: niladic	port: none	# NCRELOP (NCRop, toke.c:278, :8696), an infix operator: perl -c refuses `isa 1` in term position, so the niladic shape is the prototype's artifact.
method	core: niladic	port: none	# a keyword read as `sub` (yyl_sub, toke.c:9069); its KW_METHOD_named and KW_METHOD_anon classes are keywords, not builtin classes, so the entry stays, as catch's does.
not	core: list	port: FUNC1	# FUN1 only when a ( follows, else NOTOP (toke.c:8790); the port has FUNC1 before ( and NOTOP otherwise, and CORE.tpm's `$;` prototype reads as a list operator, which `not 1, 2` is by precedence. Both are true of different forms.
